12	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
13	
14	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
15	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
16	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
17	
18	The relative Picard functor is
19	
20	```
21	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
22	```
23	
24	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
25	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
26	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
27	against it is a natural bijection
28	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
29	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
30	
31	## The étale-sheafification route (owner decision of 2026-07-28)
32	
33	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, and
34	that is what this file's obligation is stated against —
35	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, over an **arbitrary** base field, with **no
36	hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in
37	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`PicScheme.picEt`, `picEt_isSheaf_forget`), by
38	sheafifying the relative Picard presheaf for Mathlib's big étale topology
39	localised at `Spec k`.
40	
41	Why the sheafification is not optional. The plain relative functor
42	`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
43	general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302), and a
44	representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical topology. So an
45	unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is a **false** statement, not
46	merely an unproved one. Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5** repairs it only under a
47	**section**: given one (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic for our
48	proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparisons
49	
50	```
51	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
52	```
53	
54	are bijective. That conditional route survives here as `PicEtComparisonIso`
55	(the use-site comparison class) and `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, both clearly
56	labelled as **strictly weaker than the challenge**. They are not the headline
57	and must not be reported as progress toward it.
58	
59	The two interfaces, and which one to build against:
60	
61	* `HasPicSchemeEt` / `PicSchemeEt` / `representableEt` / `groupSchemeStructureEt`
62	  — **unconditional**, the étale formulation, the target. New work goes here.
63	* `HasPicScheme` / `PicScheme` / `representable` / `groupSchemeStructure` — the
64	  legacy `picSharp`-shaped interface, whose only producer is now the
65	  conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`. Consumers quantifying over
66	  `[HasPicScheme C]` as a hypothesis remain valid and kernel-clean; they are
67	  simply conditional statements until restated against `picEt`.
68	
69	## Main results
70	
71	* `fgaPicardRepresentability` — **the project's central open obligation**:
72	  representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` over an arbitrary field, no rational
73	  point. The file's only `sorry`.
74	* `HasPicSchemeEt`, `PicSchemeEt`, `representableEt`,
75	  `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType`, `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated`,
76	  `groupSchemeStructureEt` — the unconditional étale interface derived from it.
77	* `PicEtComparisonIso`, `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — the **conditional**
78	  Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 route, strictly weaker than the challenge, not the
79	  headline.
80	* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
81	* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
82	  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
83	  quotient encoding).
84	* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
85	  scheme and the natural bijection
86	  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
87	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
88	  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
89	  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
90	* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
91	  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
92	  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
93	* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
94	  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
95	  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
96	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
97	  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
98	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.
99	
100	## Remaining obligations
101	
102	**Exactly one** statement in this file is `sorry`: `fgaPicardRepresentability`,
103	the existence of a scheme representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard
104	functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and separated and locally of finite type over `k`, for
105	an arbitrary field `k` and **no** hypothesis on `C(k)`. Mathematically this is
106	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`. It is the project's
107	central open obligation and is **expected to stay open**: discharging it needs
108	`Div` representability (Kleiman §3 `th:repDiv`, blocked on Quot) and the
109	Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma. Everything else here — the representing scheme,
110	its representability, local finiteness, separatedness and group-scheme
111	structure, and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is derived from
112	that one existence statement.
113	
114	`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
115	than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker
116	than Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`: it omits quasi-projectivity of the representing
117	scheme `Y`, for which Mathlib has no vocabulary at the pinned revision.
118	Without that hypothesis the statement is false — a Hironaka-type free
119	`ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives a smooth proper
120	equivalence relation whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is
121	not a scheme. The class must therefore be supplied at the use site, where
122	quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice is available.
123	
124	## References
125	
126	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.tex`.
127	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020): §2 Thm 2.5
128	(`th:comp` comparison under a section), §3 Def `dfn:Abel` + Thm `th:repDiv`,
129	§4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch` + Lem `lm:qt`.
130	-/

698	  rfl
699	
700	/-! ## §3. The smooth-proper quotient lemma — Altman–Kleiman descent
701	
702	The structural lemma underlying Step 4 of Kleiman §4 Thm. `th:main`: given a
703	surjection `α : Z ⟶ P` of étale sheaves with `R := Z ×_P Z` representable,
704	`Z` representable **by a quasi-projective scheme**, and the first projection
705	`R ⟶ Z` smooth and proper, the quotient `P` is representable.
706	
707	The hypothesis list expressible here is strictly weaker than Kleiman §4 Lem
708	`lm:qt`: it lacks **quasi-projectivity of `Y`**, for which Mathlib has no
709	vocabulary at the pinned revision. Without it the statement is false: a
710	Hironaka-type free `ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold
711	gives a smooth proper equivalence relation satisfying hypotheses (1)–(4)
712	whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is not a scheme. In
713	particular there is no global instance of `HasSmoothProperQuotient`; such an
714	instance would assert that every presheaf receiving any natural
715	transformation is representable.
716	
717	`HasSmoothProperQuotient α` is therefore an **explicit use-site hypothesis**:
718	the intended consumer (the FGA assembly, Step 4 of `th:main`) instantiates it
719	for the Abel-map slice `Z ⟶ P^{φ_0}_0`, where `Z` is a quasi-projective open
720	of `Div_{C/k}` and Altman–Kleiman descent genuinely applies. Supplying that
721	instance is part of the `fgaPicardRepresentability` obligation, not a standalone
722	global fact.
723	
724	Blueprint reference: `lem:smooth_proper_quotient` (Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`). -/
725	
726	/-- Hypothesis class packaging the CONCLUSION of the Altman–Kleiman
727	smooth-proper quotient lemma for a specific étale-sheaf surjection `α`:
728	that the target presheaf is representable.
729	
730	There is deliberately no global instance: an unconditional one would be a
731	false statement (see the section header). The class is supplied at the use
732	site, where the Kleiman `lm:qt` hypotheses — including quasi-projectivity of
733	the representing scheme, which the `smoothProperQuotient` statement below
734	cannot express — actually hold.
735	
736	The class is kept as the blueprint-pinned record of the Altman–Kleiman
737	`lm:qt` interface. A route to `fgaPicardRepresentability` that takes only finite
738	Galois quotients with an orbit-in-affine hypothesis sidesteps the
739	Hironaka-type counterexample above, and so needs neither this class nor
740	`smoothProperQuotient`. -/
741	class HasSmoothProperQuotient {k : Type u} [Field k]
742	    {Z P : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)}
743	    (_α : Z ⟶ P) : Prop where
744	  is_representable : P.IsRepresentable
745	
746	/-- **The smooth-proper quotient lemma — Altman–Kleiman descent of an
747	étale-sheaf surjection** (Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`).
748	
749	Let `Z, P : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1)` be presheaves and `α : Z ⟶ P` a natural
750	transformation with: (1) `Z` representable by `Y`; (2) `R := Z ×_P Z`
751	representable by `R`; (3) the first projection `π : R ⟶ Y` smooth and proper;
752	(4) `α` an étale-local surjection (every `T`-point of `P` lifts along some
753	test morphism). Then, granting the use-site hypothesis
754	`[HasSmoothProperQuotient α]` (which additionally encodes Kleiman's
755	quasi-projectivity of `Y` — see the section header for why it cannot yet be
756	stated internally), `P` is representable.
757	
758	The Lean body extracts the conclusion from the hypothesis class; the
759	mathematical content (Altman–Kleiman effective-equivalence-relation descent
760	+ EGA IV 8.11.5) lives at the use site supplying the instance. -/
761	theorem smoothProperQuotient {k : Type u} [Field k]
762	    {Z P : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)}
763	    (α : Z ⟶ P)
764	    (Y : Over (Spec (.of k)))
765	    (_hZ : Z.RepresentableBy Y)
766	    (R : Over (Spec (.of k)))
767	    (_hR : (Limits.pullback α α).RepresentableBy R)
768	    (π : R ⟶ Y)
769	    [Smooth π.left] [IsProper π.left]
770	    (_hα : ∀ ⦃T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ⦄ (p : P.obj T),
771	        ∃ (T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (e : T ⟶ T') (z : Z.obj T'),
772	          α.app T' z = P.map e p)
773	    [HasSmoothProperQuotient α] :
774	    P.IsRepresentable :=
775	  HasSmoothProperQuotient.is_representable (_α := α)
776	
777	/-! ## §4. The FGA representability theorem
778	
779	Grothendieck's existence theorem for the Picard scheme (Kleiman §4 Thm.
780	`th:main`, specialised via Cor. `cor:algsch` to `S = Spec k`, `X = C`),
781	transported through Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 to the plain relative functor under
782	the rational-point hypothesis: `picSharp C` is representable by `PicScheme C`.
783	
784	Blueprint reference: `thm:fga_pic_representability`. -/
785	
786	/-- Typeclass asserting that `picSharp C` is representable by `PicScheme C`.
787	
788	It follows from `HasPicScheme` — the representing witness is
789	`Classical.choose`-extracted, so its `choose_spec` is exactly this statement.
790	The class survives to preserve the blueprint-pinned consumer signature of
791	`representable`. -/
792	class PicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
793	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
794	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : Prop where
795	  has_representable : Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy (PicScheme C))
796	
797	/-- Existence instance for `PicSharpRepresentable`: `PicScheme C` is
798	`Classical.choose` of the `HasPicScheme` existential, and the first component
799	of `Exists.choose_spec` says precisely that the chosen scheme represents
800	`picSharp C` (the remaining components are local finiteness and
801	separatedness). The FGA content lives upstream in `fgaPicardRepresentability`. -/
802	instance instPicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k]
803	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
804	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
805	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : PicSharpRepresentable C :=
806	  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.1⟩
807	
808	/-- **FGA representability of the Picard scheme.**
809	
810	Let `k` be a field and `C` a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over
811	`k` (with, through the `HasPicScheme` hypothesis chain, a `k`-rational
812	point). Then the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}` is representable by
813	the Picard scheme `PicScheme C`: there is a natural bijection
814	
815	```
816	(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)
817	```
818	
819	for every `k`-scheme `T`. This `RepresentableBy` structure is a comparison
820	against the relative Picard functor itself, so downstream consumers
821	(tangent-space computation at the identity, `Pic⁰` degree theory) can compose
822	with its `homEquiv` to transfer line-bundle data to scheme points. -/
823	noncomputable def representable {k : Type u} [Field k]
824	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
825	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
826	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] [PicSharpRepresentable C] :
827	    (picSharp C).RepresentableBy (PicScheme C) :=
828	  Classical.choice (PicSharpRepresentable.has_representable (C := C))
829	
830	/-! ## §5. The abelian group-scheme structure
831	
832	The Picard scheme `Pic_{C/k}` inherits an abelian group-scheme structure from
833	the tensor product of invertible sheaves on `C ×_k T`: the relative Picard
834	presheaf is group-valued (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), and a representing object
835	of (the set-valued shadow of) a group-valued presheaf is canonically a group
836	object, by Yoneda transport (`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`).
837	
838	Since `picSharp` is by definition `relPresheaf ⋙ forget`, the transport
839	applies directly.
840	
841	Blueprint reference: `thm:pic_is_group_scheme` (Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs` +
842	§4 Def. `df:Psch`). -/
843	
844	/-- The multiplicative (`CommGrpCat`-valued) avatar of the relative Picard
845	presheaf, used to feed `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (whose API is
846	multiplicative). Carrier-level it is the same functor: `Multiplicative` is a
847	type synonym. -/
848	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrp {k : Type u} [Field k]
849	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
850	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
851	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
852	  PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.toCommGrp
853	
854	/-- The set-valued shadows of `picSharpCommGrp` and `picSharp` agree up to
855	the canonical `Multiplicative.ofAdd` bijection (a natural isomorphism, since
856	`Multiplicative` is carrier-preserving). -/
857	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrpForgetIso {k : Type u} [Field k]
858	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
859	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
860	    picSharp C ≅ picSharpCommGrp C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
861	  NatIso.ofComponents
862	    (fun T => Equiv.toIso (Multiplicative.ofAdd
863	      (α := ((PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T : Type (u+1)))))
864	    (fun _ => rfl)
865	
866	/-- **The Picard scheme is a commutative `k`-group scheme** — a canonical
867	`CommGrpObj` structure (i.e. `GrpObj` + `IsCommMonObj`) on `PicScheme C`,
868	obtained by Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the
869	abelian-group structure of the relative Picard presheaf
870	`PicSharp.relPresheaf` along the representability witness `representable C`.
871	Concretely: `[L] + [M] = [L ⊗ M]`, `-[L] = [L⁻¹]`, unit `[O_{C ×_k T}]`,
872	transported through `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`.
873	
874	Commutativity comes for free from the transport, so this is the full
875	abelian-group-scheme statement of the blueprint
876	(`thm:pic_is_group_scheme`). -/
877	noncomputable instance groupSchemeStructure {k : Type u} [Field k]
878	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
879	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
880	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
881	    CommGrpObj (PicScheme C) :=
882	  CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy (PicScheme C) (picSharpCommGrp C)
883	    ((representable C).ofIso (picSharpCommGrpForgetIso C))
884	
885	/-! ## §6. Local finiteness of the Picard scheme
886	
887	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): the Picard scheme is separated and locally of
888	finite type over the base. `HasPicScheme` packages local finiteness together
889	with the representability existential (one existence package, as in Kleiman's
890	theorem), so the carrier below is obtained by extraction. It is what the
891	identity-component substrate (`Picard/IdentityComponent.lean`,
892	`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent`) consumes to specialise to
893	`G = PicScheme C`. -/
894	
895	/-- Typeclass asserting that the structural morphism of the Picard scheme is
896	locally of finite type (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): `Pic_{C/k}` is a
897	disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes, hence locally of
898	finite type). The `HasPicScheme` existential carries local finiteness, so the
899	property of the `Classical.choose` witness is its second `choose_spec`
900	component; the class survives to preserve the blueprint-pinned consumer
901	signature. -/
902	class PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
903	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
904	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
905	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : Prop where
906	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType (PicScheme C).hom
907	
908	/-- Existence instance for `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`: Kleiman §4 Thm
909	`th:main`(1) makes local finiteness part of the same existence package as
910	representability, so the `HasPicScheme` existential carries it and the
911	property of the chosen witness is the second component of its `choose_spec`.
912	The instance hypothesis is `[HasPicScheme C]` rather than
913	`[HasRationalPoint C]`: the rational-point conditionality lives entirely in
914	`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` (the sole producer of `HasPicScheme C`), and any consumer able
915	to name `PicScheme C` already quantifies over `[HasPicScheme C]`. -/
916	instance instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
917	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
918	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
919	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
920	    PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C :=
921	  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.2.1⟩
922	
923	/-- Projection of `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` to the Mathlib morphism
924	property, so that instance search finds `LocallyOfFiniteType (PicScheme
925	C).hom` whenever the carrier class is in scope (as the identity-component
926	substrate requires). -/
927	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
928	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
929	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
930	    [PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
931	    LocallyOfFiniteType (PicScheme C).hom :=
932	  PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType.locallyOfFiniteType
933	
934	/-- **`Pic_{C/k}` is separated over `k`.**
935	
936	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` packages separatedness together with representability
937	and local finite type for `Pic_{C/k}` ("Then `Pic_{X/k}` is separated, ..."):
938	one existence package, as in the theorem. As with
939	`instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, we extract this property from the
940	strengthened `HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme` existential — its third
941	component — so downstream files (`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`) can consume
942	`IsSeparated (PicScheme C).hom` as a normal instance without opening the axiom
943	layer. The conditionality on `[HasRationalPoint C]` lives entirely upstream in
944	`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` (the sole producer of `HasPicScheme C`); this extraction only
945	names `[HasPicScheme C]`, as every consumer able to name `PicScheme C`
946	already does. -/
947	instance isSeparated {k : Type u} [Field k]
948	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
949	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
950	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
951	    IsSeparated (PicScheme C).hom :=
952	  (HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.2.2
953	
954	end PicScheme
955
